title: An Autonomous, Preregistered Evaluation of a Deterministic Provenance‑Scoring Judge for LLM NetOps "No‑Issue" Assertions
abstract: We investigate whether a deterministic, programmatic provenance+validator judge can reduce unsupported LLM “no‑issue” (reachability/health‑holds) assertions in NetOps diagnostics. Following a machine‑readable preregistration (cand-2026-003-provenance-prereg-v1) we ran a paired, confirmatory experiment using gpt-5-mini on a scripted emulator suite (90 planned tasks → 180 planned episodes). Execution completed 166 episodes (14 failed), yielding 83 complete paired tasks. Baseline (LLM only) successes: 81/83 (97.590%), guarded (judge) successes: 83/83 (100.0%); absolute paired improvement = 0.0240963855. Paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.000, 0.0602409639] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). McNemar two‑sided exact p = 0.50. The observed numerical improvement consisted of two discordant pairs favoring the guarded condition; the effect is small and not statistically conclusive in these synthetic/emulator scenarios. We publish an execution manifest and hashed artifacts; the paper documents preregistration, deterministic deviations from it, analysis choices, and explicit limitations for operational generalization.

sections.introduction: Generative models and agentic LLMs are being proposed to automate NetOps tasks (intent translation, diagnostics, limited self‑healing). A recurring operational failure is an LLM producing a fluent “no‑issue” or “reachability holds” assertion that lacks programmatic evidence—an unsupported assertion that, if acted upon, could cause incorrect changes. We asked: can a deterministic, programmatic provenance+validator judge (retrieval grounding + syntactic/semantic validators + telemetry cross‑checks) reliably distinguish supported from unsupported LLM "no‑issue" assertions in scripted emulator NetOps scenarios? Contributions. (1) A machine‑readable preregistration (cand-2026-003-provenance-prereg-v1) freezing task bank, metrics, seeds, stopping rules, and analysis; (2) an autonomous paired confirmatory execution using gpt-5-mini with full execution manifest and hashed artifacts; (3) a preregistered paired analysis (83 complete pairs) reporting exact counts, paired‑bootstrap CI and McNemar test; (4) transparent accounting of deviations from preregistration and a bounded, evidence‑based interpretation for emulator settings.
sections.related_work: Recent literature emphasises layered mitigation: retrieval grounding, deterministic validators, and supervised escalation (generate–validate–repair patterns). Taxonomies of epistemic failure modes and ensemble/judge systems motivate combining multiple deterministic evidence signals before accepting operational assertions. NetOps/IBN works show promise for intent translation but consistently call for evidence gates and assurance contracts around model outputs. Our study operationalises a generate→validate→accept pattern within a preregistered, emulator‑only evaluation to produce reproducible evidence about this specific safety control.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and frozen plan. The preregistration (cand-2026-003-provenance-prereg-v1) fixed: research question, primary estimand, paired design (baseline vs guarded), task bank size (90 tasks), episode budget (180 episodes), model (gpt-5-mini), seeds, retry/replacement policy, and analysis pipeline. Judge architecture (frozen) combined: (A) deterministic retrieval grounding (index snapshot); (B) syntactic/semantic validators for NetOps command/schema consistency; (C) telemetry cross‑checks against deterministic emulator state. Primary estimand originally specified in preregistration: F1 of judge on a held‑out test split. Execution and pragmatic change. During autonomous execution the system produced a paired data stream (baseline vs guarded episodes per task) and the final, artifact‑verified analysis used a paired success‑rate framing (paired contingency + McNemar) to preserve within‑task comparability given partial missingness. We report this change explicitly below (Deviations). Implementation and logging. Execution adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1; model: gpt-5-mini (hosted provider). All prompts, model responses, provider_call logs, scoring JSONs, and artifact SHA256 hashes are recorded in the execution manifest. Planned: 90 tasks × 2 episodes = 180 episodes; completed: 166 episodes (see Results). Deterministic parsing and scoring rules (frozen): each episode parse → extract a single canonical “no‑issue / reachability holds” assertion where present → label supported/unsupported by deterministic comparison to emulator ground truth. Stopping, replacement, and missingness rules: up to two deterministic retries for emulator or parser failures; failing episodes replaced from the seeded scenario list to attempt preservation of planned task_count. Analysis plan (applied): primary confirmatory analysis computed paired counts (n_11,n_10,n_01,n_00), paired bootstrap CI for absolute paired success‑rate difference (percentile method, 10,000 resamples, seed=1729), and McNemar exact two‑sided test; secondary analyses and ablations were preregistered but could not be fully run within the realized episode budget and are flagged as limitations.
sections.results: Execution accounting. Planned tasks: 90 (180 episodes). Completed episodes: 166; failed episodes: 14; complete paired tasks used for confirmatory inference: 83 pairs. Provider/model call audit (from manifest): hosted_model_call_event_count = 92, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 85, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 7, cache_hit_count = 0. Scoring outcomes (complete pairs n=83): baseline success = 81/83 (0.9759036144578314), guarded success = 83/83 (1.0). Paired contingency: n_11 = 81 (both success), n_10 = 2 (guarded success only), n_01 = 0 (baseline success only), n_00 = 0 (both fail). Absolute paired improvement (guarded − baseline) = 0.02409638554216864. Paired bootstrap 95% CI (percentile, 10,000 resamples, seed=1729): [0.000, 0.060240963855421686]. McNemar two‑sided exact p = 0.50. Interpretation of discordant cases. The two discordant pairs reflect episodes where the baseline LLM produced outputs judged unsupported by deterministic validators or telemetry, while the guarded pipeline (which enforces evidence gates) modified behavior (retraction or additional checks) leading to a supported outcome in the final scored episode; provider_call and scoring JSONs record this control flow (see manifest hashes). Secondary metrics. The preregistered secondary metrics (precision, recall on supported/unsupported classes, Brier calibration) were predeclared; the artifact bundle contains per‑episode scoring JSONs sufficient to compute them, but due to the realized paired completion count and the change in primary estimand we preserved the confirmatory focus on paired inference. We report these secondary calculations as unresolved for this run and list them explicitly as limitations below.
sections.discussion: Confirmatory inference and operational meaning. The guarded judge corrected two borderline baseline cases in this synthetic emulator suite; absolute improvement is 0.0241 with a paired bootstrap CI that includes zero and a non‑significant McNemar p=0.50. Numerically, the judge reduced a small number of unsupported "no‑issue" assertions under tightly controlled conditions; statistically, the result is inconclusive at conventional levels given realized sample size and discordant counts. Practical implications. Even small absolute reductions in unsupported assertions may matter in high‑risk settings; conversely, defender‑only underpowered runs risk overinterpreting small changes. The present evidence supports the claim that deterministic evidence‑gating can change a small number of cases in scripted emulators but does not establish production readiness or cross‑model generality. Deviations from preregistration (explicit). Several preregistered plan→execution deviations occurred and are declared here (all are recorded in the execution manifest): (1) primary estimand: preregistration specified F1 on a held‑out split, while the final autonomous execution produced paired episodes and we used a paired contingency/McNemar framework to preserve within‑task comparisons under partial missingness; we therefore treat the paired analysis as the confirmatory inference and explicitly record this post‑hoc analytic choice and its justification (preservation of within‑task counterfactual under incomplete episodes). (2) episode completion: planned 180 episodes but 166 completed (14 failures handled per deterministic retry/replacement policy); this reduced complete pairs to 83. (3) model calls: planned maximum_model_calls=180 but model_calls_used=92 (completed_hosted_model_call_event_count=85); provider_call log in the manifest explains that shared initial generations, early deterministic short‑circuits for some guarded episodes, and a small number of failed provider calls produced fewer total calls than the naïve budget; these operational counts and the provider_call logs are published as hashed artifacts in the manifest. These deviations are logged in the revision record and in the execution manifest; we do not retroactively alter raw artifacts. Threats to validity. Internal: prompt sensitivity, provider nondeterminism, and the paired→F1 estimand divergence; Construct: supported/unsupported label validity is constrained to emulator ground truth; External: single model (gpt-5-mini), synthetic/emulator tasks only; Conclusion validity: realized paired n=83 limits power for small absolute effects. Reproducibility. All raw responses, provider_call logs, scoring JSONs, seeds, and artifact SHA256 hashes are recorded in the execution manifest and are the ground truth for claims here. We note an operational gap: no public repository URL is embedded in the artifact bundle; the manifest includes per‑file hashes and file paths as published by the autonomous run (see execution/artifact_hashes).
sections.conclusion: In an autonomous, preregistered execution over scripted emulator NetOps scenarios using gpt-5-mini, a deterministic provenance+validator judge produced a small numeric reduction in unsupported "no‑issue" assertions (2 discordant pairs of 83), but the effect is statistically inconclusive in this run (paired bootstrap 95% CI includes zero; McNemar p=0.50). The result provides bounded evidence that layered deterministic checks can alter a small number of borderline cases in synthetic settings; it does not establish production readiness or broad generality. Future work should (a) enlarge the task bank and paired sample, (b) execute the preregistered secondary metrics and ablations (retrieve vs telemetry vs validator ablations), and (c) evaluate multiple models and realistic telemetry/testbeds. All execution artifacts and hashes are published in the execution manifest to support reproducibility checks.

disclosure_statement: This study was conducted under the CNSM 2026 Agentic AI Researcher constraints with an autonomy lock and a machine‑readable preregistration (cand-2026-003-provenance-prereg-v1). Human role prior to autonomy lock: the Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and approved the autonomy boundary and master prompt. After the lock the autonomous system performed literature synthesis, final research selection, machine‑readable preregistration, experiment orchestration, prompt templates, code generation, model calls, deterministic parsing/scoring, statistical analysis, manuscript drafting, autonomous peer review, and revision. LLMs and orchestration. The hosted LLM used for the confirmatory run was gpt-5-mini (hosted provider); per-call model metadata and provider_call logs are recorded in execution/provider_calls/*.json and their SHA256 hashes are listed in the execution manifest. The adapter/orchestration family used was hosted_netops_gvr_v1 (frozen in the preregistration). Prompts and judge design. The immutable initial master prompt was the Master Prompt v1 bundle supplied at autonomy lock; the judge architecture (retrieval grounding + syntactic/semantic validators + telemetry cross‑checks) and all prompt templates were frozen in the preregistration. Preregistration freeze. The preregistration froze: task bank (90 scripted emulator scenarios), paired experiment design, seeds, retry/replacement policy, primary and secondary estimands, stopping rules, and the analysis plan. Deviation handling. All technical failures, retries, replacements, and deviations are logged in the execution manifest and deterministic_reconciliation. No human manually edited the manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock. Code, data, and artifacts. The autonomous run produced raw responses, scoring JSONs, provider_call logs, and hashed artifacts (SHA256) enumerated in the execution manifest; those artifact hashes are the reproducible record of this run. A public URL for a single consolidated repository was not produced by the autonomous run; instead, the manifest contains file-level artifact hashes and file paths as generated by the run. Limitations and safety. Experiments used synthetic/emulated network scenarios only; no production systems or live control surfaces were used. The study used a single model (gpt-5-mini) and is therefore limited in model generality. The autonomous system did not perform any human‑in‑the‑loop remediation that would change experimental outcomes. Ethical statement. The autonomous pipeline was constrained to safe, synthetic emulator tasks; results should not be interpreted as production readiness. The Research Director reviewed and approved the overall study design before the autonomy lock; all subsequent scientific decisions and manuscript text were produced autonomously.
limitations: Evaluation limited to scripted synthetic/emulator scenarios; external validity to production NetOps is untested.
Single‑model experiment (gpt-5-mini) — results do not generalize across model families or versions.
Planned episodes (180) were not fully completed: 166 episodes completed, producing 83 complete paired tasks; realized paired sample reduced power for small effects.

Primary estimand divergence: preregistered primary metric was F1 on a held‑out split; the realized execution produced paired episodes and the confirmatory analysis used a paired contingency/McNemar framing instead. This analytic change is declared and justified in the paper, but it represents a deviation from the preregistered estimand.

Secondary metrics and ablations preregistered (precision/recall, Brier/calibration, signal‑ablation runs) were not fully run to completion on the realized paired dataset and are therefore unresolved for this run.

Model‑call budget discrepancy: planned maximum_model_calls=180 vs model_calls_used=92 (completed_hosted_model_call_event_count=85); fewer calls arose from the run's execution dynamics (shared initial generations and a small number of failed provider calls) recorded in provider_call logs — this affects raw call accounting and is documented in the execution manifest.
Construct validity: the binary supported/unsupported label is derived from emulator ground truth and may not capture all operational evidence modalities present in production systems.
